title: Al-Kafirun 109:4-6 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: An-Nasr, Al-Kafirun and reading joined words
source: Written for quran/y1 lesson 33 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Kafirun 109:4-6 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 33. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَلَآ أَنَا۠ عَابِدٌۭ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ (٤) وَلَآ أَنتُمْ عَٰبِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ (٥) لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِىَ دِينِ (٦)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship.
Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship.
For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Kafirun 109:4-6 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 109:4-6 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Say Al-Kafirun 1 to 6 to a grown-up.
What is the last ayah about?
questions.a: A) Each has their own religion. 109:6: 'For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.'

questions.q: Al-Kafirun 109:6: «لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Al-Kafirun ends: 'For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.' What does it mean to be kind to people but firm in our worship?
questions.a: We are kind and fair to everyone, but we only worship Allah and do not join other worship.
